reports.title: Gut bacteria and oxidative stress linked to alpha-synuclein aggregation
reports.summary: The findings study whether gut microbial exposures and oxidative stress increase alpha-synuclein aggregation, a process tied to parkinsonian pathology. Both papers report increased alpha-synuclein aggregation, with paper strength 3 for the Akkermansia muciniphila and oxidative stress claims and strength 2 for the bacterial protein claim. The claims do not conflict, since all four report an increase. Press coverage is mixed: the oxidative stress claim was understated (press 2 vs paper 3), and the bacterial protein claim was overstated (press 3 vs paper 2). The Akkermansia claims have no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Akkermansia muciniphila conditioned medium is stated to increase alpha-synuclein aggregation.
Oral administration of Akkermansia muciniphila grown without mucin is stated to increase alpha-synuclein aggregation in cholecystokinin-positive enteroendocrine cells.
Oxidative stress is stated to increase alpha-synuclein aggregation.
Bacterial proteins may increase alpha-synuclein aggregation in enteroendocrine cells.

reports.title: Handedness and lateral biases in spatial ability and social touch
reports.summary: These findings study how handedness relates to spatial navigation ability and to lateral biases in cradling and social touch. The large navigation study (P1) reports no reliable handedness difference across 41 countries, while a small age-related gap favoring left-handers over 64 is judged likely due to selection bias. The cradling meta-analysis (P2) reports that left-handers show a less pronounced leftward bias than right-handers and that handedness and sex contribute to cradling bias, and the social touch review (P3) reports that lateral biases are influenced but not fully determined by handedness. Across papers the handedness effects on lateral bias are not contradictory, but the spatial ability claims conflict in that one reports a no-effect result beside a weak increase for older participants. All press-matched claims were aligned with their papers' strength, and the remaining claims had no matched press coverage.

key_findings.text: Handedness shows no reliable association with spatial navigation ability across 41 countries, with the age-over-64 gap judged likely due to selection bias.
Left-handers show a less pronounced leftward cradling bias than right-handers, and males are less lateralized than females.
Handedness and sex may contribute to a cradling population bias.
Lateral biases in social touch are influenced, but not fully determined, by handedness.
A small gap favoring left-handers over right-handers appears in participants over 64 years old.

reports.title: Neural circuits of fear, learning, memory retrieval, and burst firing
reports.summary: These findings study neural mechanisms of fear, associative learning, memory retrieval and escape in mice and human recordings, centred on burst firing, engram excitability and defined neuron populations. Papers agree that manipulating specific neuron populations changes fear or escape behaviour and that bursting relates to learning and retrieval. The conflicts are limited: regular spike trains had no effect on retrieval while bursts did, and chord-specific bursting was reported with no response to constituent tones. Of the nine claims with a press match, eight were aligned with the paper's strength, while two were overstated: the CREB fear claim (C3) and the trained-sound burst claim (C10).

key_findings.text: Optogenetic manipulation of defined neuron populations directly altered fear or escape behaviour, with stimulation of fear-acquisition neurons increasing fear and stimulation of vLGN abolishing escape.
Bursts were sufficient to retrieve learned behaviour, whereas regular spike trains showed no effect on retrieval.
Learning was associated with burst firing and enhanced dendritic excitability, and disrupting dendritic activity suppressed learning.
Increased CREB expression in amygdala Crh neurons increased fear expression and inhibited extinction, and CREB may function as a molecular switch regulating fear and its extinction.

Auditory cortex neurons showed bursting to trained multitone chords, with no response to constituent tones; the trained sound was associated with burst firing, and such bursts were largely absent in untrained mice.

reports.title: Neural activity patterns linked to spatial distance and psychiatric diagnosis
reports.summary: This community groups two papers that each study neural activity patterns, one examining spatial distance in a mentally reconstructed space and one examining psychiatric diagnosis. The two findings have different exposures and outcomes, so the papers neither agree nor conflict. In P1, Euclidean distance between people in a mentally reconstructed 2-D space was associated with multivariate activity patterns in HC, EC and vmPFC/mOFC, with the direction unclear. In P2, cluster membership showed no association found with diagnosis or scan site. No press statement was matched to either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers' findings.

key_findings.text: Euclidean distance in a mentally reconstructed 2-D space was associated with neural activity patterns in HC, EC and vmPFC/mOFC, with the direction unclear.
No association was found between diagnosis and neural activity pattern cluster membership in people with and without severe mental illness.

reports.title: 2-Deoxyglucose and CLC-3 disruption linked to reduced epileptiform activity
reports.summary: These findings study whether 2-deoxyglucose after traumatic brain injury and CLC-3 chloride channel loss affect epileptiform activity in the brain. All three claims report a decrease in epileptiform activity, so no conflicting directions or null results appear. The two 2-deoxyglucose claims (C1, C3) use direct causal wording at strength 3, while the CLC-3 knockout claim (C2) is only correlational at strength 1. Press releases matched two claims (C2, C3), and both were aligned with the paper's strength; the in vitro 2-deoxyglucose claim (C1) had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: 2-Deoxyglucose reduces epileptiform activity after traumatic brain injury, with direct causal wording in both the in vitro and in vivo studies.
CLC-3 knockout is associated with reduced epileptiform activity in neonatal neurons.

reports.title: Non-drug therapies and electrical stimulation linked to patient-reported global improvement
reports.summary: The two findings study whether non-drug interventions improve patient global impression of change (PGIC), one a digital behavioural therapy trial in fibromyalgia and one a pilot of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for female sexual dysfunction. Both papers report increases in PGIC and are associated at strength 1, so their wording is correlational rather than causal. No press statement was matched to either paper, so press coverage cannot be compared. The two studies cover different conditions and interventions, so the community offers limited evidence beyond these two papers.

key_findings.text: In a fibromyalgia trial, acceptance and commitment therapy was associated with an increase in patient global impression of change, with 71% of ACT participants improved versus 22% of active controls at 12 weeks.
In a pilot study of female sexual dysfunction, transcutaneous electric nerve stimulation was associated with a significant increase in patient global impression of change.

reports.title: Type 2 diabetes and reward coding in animal ACC and hippocampus
reports.summary: The claims mostly concern how type 2 diabetes affects reward and spatial processing in animal anterior cingulate and hippocampal activity, alongside a few unrelated papers on ADHD genetics, music reward, and picky eating. Papers from the diabetes study agree that hyperglycemia alters reward coding, with the strongest wording describing a causal reduction in reward coding and a reduced post-reinforcement pause. Spatial coding results are less consistent, with higher spatial information scores reported alongside an unclear direction of change in spatial coding properties, and a separate claim reports no association with behavioral accuracy. Press coverage was understated for three diabetes claims and aligned for two, while the claim that rewards for eating may increase picky eating was overstated. Outside the diabetes theme, the music reward study found no association between axial diffusivity and reward-task activity, and the ADHD study reports an association with type 2 diabetes.

key_findings.text: Type 2 diabetes leads to reward coding deficits and a muted reward location representation in animal ACC and hippocampus.
Type 2 diabetes is associated with higher spatial information scores in ACC neurons and a differential change in spatial coding properties.
No association was found between type 2 diabetes and behavioral accuracy, while hyperglycemic animals were associated with spending less time at the reward site.
ADHD genetic liability is associated with an increase in type 2 diabetes among adults in electronic health records.
Rewards for eating may increase picky eating in children, according to a scoping review.

reports.title: Brain oscillations, neuromodulation, cannabidiol, and adverse events across studies
reports.summary: This community is heterogeneous, linking brain oscillations (alpha, beta, theta) with aging, TMS and rTMS neuromodulation, cannabidiol, and treatment safety reporting. Within the aging findings, older adults showed stronger alpha and beta oscillations (C1, C36), and aging was associated with decreased vesicle-mediated transport (C37). Cannabidiol results diverge: a dog trial found similar responder proportions (C4), while a human trial simulation associated cannabidiol with reduced drop-seizure frequency through a clobazam interaction (C27). Most safety claims report no serious adverse events (C7, C17, C26, C29, C32, C34), but pembrolizumab and dog cannabidiol studies report adverse events (C21, C39). Press coverage was mostly aligned with the papers, with overstated labels on C8, C27 and C30 and understated labels on C6 and C10; no retracted papers appear.

key_findings.text: Older age was associated with stronger alpha and beta oscillations in prefrontal and other cortical regions during working memory encoding, maintenance and retrieval.

Fronto-striatal TMS directly altered music-induced pleasure, with inhibition reducing pleasure and motivation in one study, while anterior prefrontal stimulation directly increased metacognitive ability in another.

Several trials reported no serious adverse events, whereas a pembrolizumab study was associated with grade-3 or higher treatment-related adverse events and a cannabidiol dog study reported ataxia in two dogs.

Cannabidiol findings conflict: a dog trial found no difference in responder proportions, while a human simulation associated cannabidiol with reduced drop-seizure frequency via a clobazam interaction.

Theta-band activity was linked to memory and language processes, with syntactic alignment increasing theta synchronization and amygdala-hippocampal theta coupling associated with successful emotional pattern separation.

reports.title: Migraine drugs, nitroglycerin, and treatments with pain outcomes
reports.summary: This community groups 12 findings from six papers that study pain as an outcome, including migraine drug trials, HDAC6 and nitroglycerin preclinical models, couple therapy for vulvodynia, selumetinib for neurofibromas, nursing facility admissions, and post-COVID symptoms. Within migraine, the network meta-analysis associates eletriptan and ibuprofen with sustained pain freedom, and reports that triptans overall were more efficacious than lasmiditan, rimegepant, and ubrogepant. Other papers report pain reductions from couple therapy (C3) and HDAC6 inhibition in a preclinical model (C2), while the selumetinib pain decrease is only correlational (C4). Pain-related links in admissions (C5) and post-exertional malaise (C6) study different exposures and are not directly comparable to the treatment findings. Press coverage matched seven of the twelve claims, all labeled aligned, and the five unmatched claims had no press statement; no papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Eletriptan and ibuprofen were the most efficacious interventions for sustained pain freedom in the migraine network meta-analysis.
All active migraine interventions were superior to placebo for pain freedom at two hours.
In head-to-head comparisons, eletriptan was the most effective drug for pain freedom at two hours.
HDAC6 inhibition reversed nitroglycerin-induced migraine-associated pain in a preclinical model.
Cognitive-behavioral couple therapy produced greater pain-related improvements than lidocaine for women with provoked vestibulodynia.

reports.title: Face masks and facial movement kinematics in emotion recognition
reports.summary: The findings study how face coverings and facial movement affect the recognition of facial emotions. Paper P1 reports that a surgical mask impaired emotion recognition, and that a transparent mask moderated this impairment compared with a surgical mask. Paper P2 reports that facial movement kinematics are associated with emotion recognition, but it does not compare against masks, so the two papers do not conflict. Press coverage of P1's surgical mask finding was labeled understated, its transparent mask finding was labeled aligned, and no press statement was matched to P2.

key_findings.text: Wearing a surgical mask impaired the recognition and perceived intensity of facial emotions.
A transparent mask moderated the impairment seen with a surgical mask.
Facial movement kinematics are associated with emotion recognition, adding value independent of other factors.

reports.title: Neural activity, epilepsy, and Parkinson's studies across exposures and interventions
reports.summary: The claims cover a broad set of exposures and outcomes, including stress, infection, drugs, gene manipulations, and brain-disease outcomes such as epilepsy and Parkinson's disease, drawn from 40 of 68 community claims. Losartan was reported to enhance radiation efficacy and reduce brain edema in NF2 models, and gluconate may suppress seizure activity in developing brains. Papers conflict on stress: predator stress was associated with increased neural activity, while psychological stress was associated with decreased neural activity. Parkinson's findings also diverge, with infection associated with increased risk and hearing loss showing no association found. Across the community, press coverage was aligned for 21 matched claims, overstated for 5 and understated for 5.

key_findings.text: Losartan enhances the efficacy of radiation therapy and reduces brain edema in NF2 mouse models.
Gluconate may suppress neonatal seizure activity by inhibiting CLC-3 chloride channels.
Predator stress is associated with increased neural activity, whereas psychological stress is associated with decreased neural activity, so the two studies point in opposite directions.
Hospital-treated infection is associated with increased Parkinson's disease risk, while hearing impairment shows no association found with Parkinson's disease.
Subthalamic nucleus activity may decrease cortico-spinal excitability, though press coverage described this effect more strongly than the paper did.

reports.title: Autism genetics, interventions, and neuroimaging across psychiatric and neurological conditions
reports.summary: The community covers autism genetics, autism interventions and outcomes, and brain-imaging findings in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, dementia, and other neurological conditions, so it is topically mixed. Most of the 40 claims shown are autism-related and are stated as associations (strength 1), while only a few are direct causal statements. Papers agree that autism is linked to genetic risk and that behavioral interventions are associated with better social outcomes. Results diverge where a null finding sits beside positive ones, such as no correlation with illness duration in one schizophrenia subtype (C8) and no difference in self-harm for early psychosis intervention users (C32). Among the claims shown, press coverage was mostly aligned with the papers, with the singing study (C5) and high-fat diet study (C24) overstated, and the anti-NRXN1α autoantibody (C20) and SUV39H2 (C39) claims understated in some press releases.

key_findings.text: Autism polygenic scores and genetic correlations are associated with childhood trauma, self-harm ideation, and self-harm.
Gene variants are associated with autism spectrum disorder across large sequencing cohorts.

Behavioral interventions are associated with improved social emotional and challenging behavior outcomes, and naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions are reported to improve social communication.

Anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies transferred from patients with schizophrenia cause schizophrenia-related pathology in mice, a direct causal claim that press releases stated in understated form for one release.

reports.title: Astrocyte activation, TRIF signaling, and survival in ALS mice
reports.summary: The findings cover astrocyte activation in relation to TRIF signaling, survival in ALS mice, and diffusion MRI signal. In the TRIF study, aberrantly activated astrocytes are associated with lower survival, and TRIF deficiency is associated with more reactive astrocytes. A conditional claim says the TRIF pathway may reduce astrocyte activation. The diffusion MRI study associates astrocyte activation with a diffusion signal, but the direction of that link is unclear, so it does not address the ALS findings. Press coverage was aligned for the astrocyte survival and TRIF deficiency claims and overstated for the TRIF pathway claim, where press stated the effect more strongly than the paper's conditional wording.

key_findings.text: Aberrantly activated astrocytes are associated with lower survival time in TRIF-deficient ALS mice.
TRIF deficiency is associated with an increase in reactive astrocytes in ALS mice.
The TRIF pathway may reduce astrocyte activation, a conditional claim that press coverage overstated as a stronger effect.
Diffusion MRI signal is associated with microglia and astrocyte activation in rat models, with an unclear direction of effect.

reports.title: Sleep responses to stress, social pressure, and chromosome dynamics
reports.summary: The findings study how sleep responds to stress and social or ecological pressure, how sleep affects chromosome dynamics and cortical plasticity, and a few other exposures in mice, zebrafish, baboons, and humans. Stress-induced sleep in mice is linked to VTA GABA-somatostatin cells (C1, C9, C13), and sleep is reported to increase chromosome dynamics in zebrafish neurons (C2, C10). Sleep is reported to restore cortical performance and criticality (C4, C5, C12), while wild baboon studies report that social and ecological pressures interfere with sleep homeostasis (C3, C11). Press coverage was aligned with the paper for most matched claims, understated for C8, C9 and C12, and overstated for the corticosterone and anxiety claims C16 and C17, which rest on a weaker associational paper strength.

key_findings.text: Social defeat stress induces sleep in mice, and lesioning VTA GABA-somatostatin cells abolishes this stress-induced sleep.
Sleep increases chromosome dynamics in individual zebrafish neurons, while no association was found in two other cell types.
Sleep restores cortical performance and critical dynamics, which waking experience progressively disrupts.
Ecological and social pressures interfere with homeostatic sleep regulation in wild baboons.
No association was found between sleep loss and more intense sleep bouts.

reports.title: Long COVID risk factors, symptoms, inflammation, and vaccination evidence
reports.summary: The claims cover long COVID (post-COVID condition) and its links to vaccination, prior infection, variant, age, sex, asthma, rhinitis, inflammation, cognition, and physical function, though many shown claims concern unrelated topics such as baboon sleep, mouse apnea, schizophrenia subtypes, and socioeconomic mobility. The papers conflict on vaccination: one reports that vaccination results in lower long COVID rates, while another finds no association between vaccination and risk. They also conflict on age, with one study reporting higher susceptibility in older participants and another reporting higher risk under 50 years. Most cohort findings are only associations, with asthma and rhinitis and blood-brain barrier disruption cited as associations rather than causes. Press coverage overstated the paper's strength for several shown claims (C4, C10, C15, C23, C31) and understated it for C11, C12, and C36, while across the full set press labels were 25 aligned, 8 overstated, and 4 understated among 34 matched claims.

key_findings.text: Vaccination was stated to result in lower long COVID rates, while another study found no association between vaccination and post-COVID-19 risk.
Older age and female sex were associated with long COVID risk, although one study reported higher risk in participants under 50 years.

Persistent long COVID was associated with lower neurocognitive test performance, more subjective cognitive disturbance, and reduced maximal oxygen consumption, and blood-brain barrier disruption was associated with long COVID brain fog.
Pre-existing asthma and rhinitis were associated with increased long COVID risk, though the evidence was rated very low certainty.
Persistent inflammation and neutrophil activation signatures were associated with long COVID subsets, and pre-infection inflammation may contribute to post-acute sequelae.

reports.title: Interventions extending lifespan in neurodegeneration and tumor-bearing hosts
reports.summary: This community covers two unrelated studies that both report an intervention increasing lifespan: Syt13 gene therapy in mouse models of motor neuron disease (P1) and STAT inhibition in the blood-brain barrier of tumor-bearing hosts (P2). Both papers use direct causal wording at strength 3, so no papers disagree and no null results appear. Press coverage of the STAT inhibition finding (C2) is aligned with the paper, while press coverage of the Syt13 finding (C1) is aligned in one statement and understated in another (press 1 vs paper 3). No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Syt13 gene therapy prolongs the lifespan of ALS mice by 14% and SMA mice by 50%.
Inhibiting STAT in the blood-brain barrier extends the lifespan of tumor-bearing hosts.
Press statements about the Syt13 finding were understated in one instance relative to the paper's direct causal wording.

reports.title: Review of material and post-exertional malaise, each linked to test performance
reports.summary: This community groups two findings from unrelated studies that share only the outcome label test performance: one on students' reported review of material and one on post-exertional malaise in adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome. In P1, being tested made students more likely to report reviewing the material, but no association found was reported between those reports and test performance. In P2, patients with persistent PCS and PEM were associated with worse results in almost all tests, with more pain symptoms. The two findings do not conflict in direction, but they study different exposures, so they should not be read as a combined answer on test performance. Neither claim has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers.

key_findings.text: Being tested made students more likely to report reviewing the material, but such reports were not associated with better test performance.
Patients with persistent PCS and PEM were associated with worse results in almost all tests.

reports.title: tDCS and training effects on appetite, psychomotor performance, and cognition
reports.summary: This community groups five findings on transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and training, with outcomes including appetite, psychomotor performance, approach motivation, motor learning, and cognitive test scores. Two appetite findings from the same trial conflict: tDCS was associated with reduced appetite in Met-carriers (C1) and with a paradoxical rise in appetite in Met non-carriers (C6). For psychomotor performance, the esports study states that tDCS increases performance (C2) and that training may increase it (C7). Other studies report an association between motor learning gains and decreased brain activation (C4), an association between lower digit symbol scores and non-US-born, Spanish-speaking status (C5), and an unclear direction for frontal stimulation effects on approach emotions (C3). Press labels were aligned for all four claims with a press match, and the esports tDCS claim also drew two understated press statements.

key_findings.text: The esports study states that tDCS increases psychomotor performance, and press statements understated this claim twice.
Training may increase psychomotor performance across expertise levels, according to the esports study.
tDCS was associated with reduced appetite in Met-carriers, while Met non-carriers showed a delayed paradoxical rise in appetite in the same trial.
Handedness predicted whether frontal stimulation increased or decreased approach-related emotions, so the direction of effect is unclear.
Better post-intervention task performance was associated with decreased activation in the anterior cingulate, paracingulate and cerebellum.

reports.title: Interventions and lesion size after brain, spinal cord injury, and stroke
reports.summary: These two claims study whether interventions change lesion size after neurological injury, one in brain injury and stroke and one in cervical spinal cord injury. The findings do not agree: low-dose ionizing radiation was reported to decrease lesion size after TBI and photothrombotic stroke, while BDNF hydrogel showed no association with lesion size. Because the claims involve different exposures and injury sites, they do not form a direct conflict on the same question. Press coverage was matched only for the radiation claim, and it was labelled understated relative to the paper's wording. No press match was found for the BDNF claim, and neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Low-dose ionizing radiation reduced lesion size and reversed motor deficits after TBI and photothrombotic stroke.
No association was found between local BDNF hydrogel delivery and lesion size or motor neuron degeneration in the injured cervical spinal cord.
Press coverage of the low-dose radiation finding was understated relative to the strength of the paper's wording.

reports.title: Microglial phagocytosis after low-dose radiation and RXRα in brain injury
reports.summary: These claims study how microglial phagocytosis changes after brain injury or stroke, through low-dose ionizing radiation and through RXRα. Both papers report increased phagocytosis, so they agree in direction and no null or opposing result appears. The RXRα claim is stated as a direct causal relationship, while the low-dose radiation claim is only correlational. Press coverage matched only the RXRα claim, with one statement understated relative to the paper and another aligned with it, and the radiation claim had no press match.

key_findings.text: RXRα promotes microglial phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons, shown in cultured microglia.
Low-dose ionizing radiation is associated with increased microglial phagocytosis and chemotactic capacity in live-cell assays.
Press statements about the RXRα finding were understated in one case and aligned in another, and no press statement matched the low-dose radiation finding.

reports.title: Microglia, fatigue, and neuroinflammation outcomes across MS, stroke, and neurodegeneration studies
reports.summary: This community groups 40 of 56 findings from 23 papers that link microglia, neuroinflammation, and fatigue to outcomes such as recovery, neuronal activity, and plaque clearance, with fatigue findings drawn from MS, Parkinson's disease, and a CBT/modafinil trial. Within the fatigue findings, the CBT and modafinil trial reports within-group MFIS reductions (C2, C39) but no between-group difference (C25), while microglial activation in MS and inflammatory markers in early Parkinson's disease are associated with fatigue (C4, C30) and an immune response "may" contribute (C7). Microglia-recovery findings conflict in part: one paper reports that depleting microglia abolished low-dose radiation's motor benefit (C9), and another reports that removing microglia had little effect on traumatic brain injury outcome while inducing microglial turnover aided recovery (C26, C40). Press coverage was mostly aligned with the papers (23 aligned), with 3 overstated labels (including C10) and 2 understated labels (C29, C31). No claims in this community come from retracted papers.

key_findings.text: Inducing microglial turnover is reported to aid recovery after brain injury, while simply removing microglia showed little effect on injury outcome.
Depleting cortical microglia and macrophages completely abolished the motor recovery benefit of low-dose ionizing radiation in stroke mice.
CBT and modafinil were associated with within-group fatigue reductions in multiple sclerosis, but change did not differ between groups.
Microglial activation and higher inflammatory markers were associated with fatigue, while brain lesion load showed no correlation with fatigue.
TAM receptor signaling directly mediates microglial engulfment of amyloid plaques, and TREM2 is required for Aβ-induced microglial migration and proliferation.

reports.title: Blood-brain barrier breakdown, obesity, memory, and neuroinflammation across mixed studies
reports.summary: This community holds 40 of 63 findings, drawn from 34 papers, that mostly concern blood-brain barrier (BBB) function, memory, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration, and many of the topics are unrelated to one another. Several papers agree that BBB permeability rises with obesity or insulin resistance and that targeting the endothelium can protect or restore barrier function. Where papers conflict, null results sit beside positive ones: targeted memory reactivation improved memory (C37) while unilateral olfactory stimulation without contextual odor showed no effect (C3), and testing had no effect on unstudied questions (C39). Among the shown claims, press labels are overstated for C6, C17, C27, C30, C31 and C35, understated for C1, C22 and C37, and aligned for the rest, and across all 63 claims the stats give 11 overstated, 7 understated and 17 aligned. No retracted papers appear among the shown claims.

key_findings.text: Obesity increased BBB permeability, and endothelial Adora2a deletion protected against BBB breakdown in mice with diet-induced insulin resistance.
Recombinant SPOCK1 partially restores BBB function, and altered mucin-domain glycoproteins dysregulate BBB function.
BBB damage is linked to host morbidity in a tumor model, and infection is associated with BBB damage and may trigger neurodegenerative disease.
Targeted memory reactivation during sleep improved memory for words, whereas unilateral olfactory stimulation without contextual odor showed no effect on memory.

Reducing neuroinflammation is linked to cognitive and motor benefits: A11 ameliorated neuroinflammation with improved cognition, neuroinflammation may aid motor recovery, and exercise may mitigate the effects of stress on hippocampal function.

reports.title: Xenon and 2-deoxyglucose effects on neuronal loss after brain injury
reports.summary: This community covers two studies of treatments after traumatic brain injury, examining xenon and 2-deoxyglucose and their effects on neuronal loss. Both papers report a decrease in neuronal loss with direct causal wording, so the claims in this community do not conflict. P1 reports that xenon reduced neuronal loss in the contralateral hippocampal CA1 and dentate gyrus at 20 months. P2 reports that 2-deoxyglucose attenuated the loss of parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons, and its press coverage was aligned with the paper's strength. No press statement was matched to the xenon finding, so press coverage cannot be compared for it.

key_findings.text: Xenon reduced neuronal loss in the contralateral hippocampal CA1 and dentate gyrus after traumatic brain injury.
2-deoxyglucose attenuated the loss of parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons after traumatic brain injury, and its press coverage was aligned with the paper.

reports.title: Expectancy, learning, and reward signals across neural and behavioral studies
reports.summary: These five papers examine musical reward prediction errors, mouse prefrontal category learning, central amygdala coding of salient events, expectancy effects on risk-taking, and learning differences in paranoia. The directional claims all point the same way, with no opposing directions and no null results (strength 0), but the paranoia claim C5 has an unclear direction and is associated only with learning differences. Strength is mostly correlational (C2, C4, C5, C7 at 1) or direct causal (C3, C6, C8, C9 at 3), with one conditional claim (C1 at 2). Press coverage overstated three claims (C1, C4, C9), aligned four (C1, C2, C4, C6), and understated the amygdala claim C3, while C5, C7 and C8 had no press match. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Expectancy supports learning in the musical reward study.
Musical stimuli elicit reward prediction errors without apparent biological value.
Somatostatin-expressing central amygdala neurons are essential for learning, a claim press coverage understated.
Learning is associated with a category representation in mouse prefrontal cortex that is gradually acquired.
Expectancy is associated with increased risk-taking, conditional on heightened expectancy, in human augmentation.

reports.title: Brain stimulation, sleep, and memory outcomes across neuroscience studies
reports.summary: This community groups 17 neuroscience papers that link brain exposures such as hippocampal sharp wave-ripples, fixation reinstatement, neural differentiation, and corpus callosum integrity to outcomes such as memory performance, glucose concentration, and slow-wave propagation. Most relationships are rated correlational (strength 1), with nine direct causal and one conditional causal claim. Papers conflict on striatal AMPA receptor potentiation and spike-and-wave discharges, where one claim reports suppression and another reports no association, and on the Sans Forgetica font, where one claim reports impaired memory and another reports no effect. Press labels across the community are 11 aligned, 4 overstated (C3, C5, C20, C24), and 2 understated (C7, C30), and no papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Hippocampal sharp wave-ripple clusters were associated with a decrease in peripheral glucose concentration, and press coverage overstated this finding in some reports.
Older adults showed greater delay-period fixation reinstatement, and this reinstatement supported age-equivalent visuospatial memory task performance.
Greater neural differentiation and reinstatement in superagers were associated with superior memory performance.

Pharmacological potentiation of striatal AMPA receptors directly suppresses spike-and-wave discharges, while another claim found no association between AMPA receptor potentiation and these discharges.
The Sans Forgetica font may impair memory performance, while another claim finds no effect of the font on memory.

reports.title: Interventions and Lewy body pathology effects on motor function outcomes
reports.summary: These findings study how several exposures relate to motor function outcomes, including TFE3 overexpression in a Parkinson's model, Lewy body pathology in cognitively impaired individuals, lipopolysaccharide with training in chronic spinal cord injury, and remote limb conditioning after stroke. The two interventional studies both report direct causal increases in motor function, while Lewy body pathology is only associated with worse motor function. Because the claims involve different exposures and populations, they do not directly conflict with one another. Only one claim, the remote limb conditioning finding, had a matched press statement, and its press strength aligned with the paper's strength. The other three claims had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: TFE3 overexpression is reported to directly restore motor function in an α-synuclein overexpression model of Parkinson's disease.
Remote limb conditioning is reported to directly increase motor and gait function in chronic stroke, and press coverage of this finding aligned with the paper's strength.
Systemic lipopolysaccharide combined with high-intensity training is reported to directly restore original motor function in chronic spinal cord injury.
Lewy body pathology is associated with worse motor function in cognitively impaired individuals, but not with amyloid-β or tau pathology in the cross-sectional analysis.

reports.title: Autophagy impairment and aggregate clearance in neurodegeneration: microglia, CCR5, TFE3
reports.summary: The findings study autophagy, the cellular pathway that clears toxic aggregate-prone proteins, in neurodegenerative disease models. Paper P1 reports that activated microglia decrease neuronal autophagy, and that CCR5 activation decreases autophagy while CCR5 inhibition increases it. Paper P2 reports that TFE3 increases autophagy and reduces alpha-synuclein aggregation in a Parkinson's model, so the two papers point in the same direction on autophagy. All four claims are stated at direct causal strength, and the three claims with a press match are labelled aligned, meaning press statements matched the papers' strength. The one claim without a press match is C1, on activated microglia.

key_findings.text: CCR5 activation decreases neuronal autophagy, and CCR5 inhibition increases it, in P1.
TFE3 increases autophagy and reduces alpha-synuclein aggregation in the AAV-alpha-synuclein Parkinson's model in P2.
Activated microglia decrease neuronal autophagy in P1.

reports.title: Ageing and reduced brain fluid clearance and glycocalyx dysregulation
reports.summary: These findings study how ageing relates to brain fluid clearance and the brain's blood vessel lining. Two Nature papers are included, and each states its relationship at strength 1, meaning 'associated with'. P1 links ageing to a decrease in the glymphatic system and in cerebrospinal fluid drainage, while P2 reports the brain endothelial glycocalyx is dysregulated during ageing, with the direction left unclear. The papers do not conflict, since they study different outcomes. For the P1 glymphatic claim, press coverage carried one aligned label and one overstated label, and the CSF drainage claim and the P2 glycocalyx claim had no press match.

key_findings.text: Ageing is associated with a decrease in glymphatic system function and impaired cerebrospinal fluid drainage in mouse meningeal lymphatic vessels.
Ageing is associated with the brain endothelial glycocalyx being highly dysregulated, with the direction of change not specified.

reports.title: COVID-19 post-acute syndrome: iron, immune cells, brain metabolism
reports.summary: These claims study post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PASC) and its links to iron and immune markers, brain glucose metabolism, and education, plus one placebo-response study that does not concern PASC. Paper P1 associates a multivariate biomarker signature with PASC, and also associates PASC with lower dendritic cell counts and with lymphopenia. Findings on brain metabolism conflict: C2 reports no association between PASC and brain glucose metabolism, while C6 associates PASC with limbic and subcortical glucose decrease. Press coverage matched only two claims (C1 and C4), and both were aligned with their papers' strength. The placebo study (C3) and the education finding (C4) each rest on a single claim with no cross-paper agreement, and no papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: PASC is associated with a multivariate signature of unresolving inflammation, anemia, low serum iron, altered iron-homeostasis gene expression and stress erythropoiesis.
PASC is associated with decreased dendritic cell counts and with increased lymphopenia.

Evidence on brain glucose metabolism conflicts: one P2 claim reports no association found between PASC and brain glucose metabolism, while another associates PASC with limbic and subcortical glucose decrease.
New PCS symptoms after initial recovery are associated with an intercurrent secondary SARS-CoV-2 infection and educational status.
Placebo response is associated with subcortical limbic volume asymmetry, sensorimotor cortical thickness and prefrontal functional coupling, a finding unrelated to PASC.

reports.title: Frailty, cognition, deep brain stimulation, and exercise: mixed outcomes across studies
reports.summary: These claims span frailty and mortality, cognition, deep brain stimulation, depression-related readmission, and exercise, so the community is heterogeneous rather than one clear topic. Frailty claims mostly point the same way, with higher mortality, hospitalization, and cognitive decline, although P4 reports no significant difference for mild frailty (C4). Most claims are associational (strength 1), and direct causal wording appears only in the mouse and stimulation studies (C8, C12, C15, C34). Among the shown claims, press overstated C4 and C36 and understated C8 and C15, while the remaining claims were aligned with their papers. No retracted papers appear in this set.

key_findings.text: Frailty was associated with higher mortality, hospitalization, acute care use, and cognitive decline in several studies.
Depression-focused post-discharge treatment was associated with fewer hospital readmissions.
Anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies reduced cognition in mice, and sensory gamma entrainment improved cognitive function in mouse models.
Exercise mode showed no clear effect on cognition, while exercise was associated with improved cognition in Parkinson's disease.
Cingulum bundle stimulation enhanced positive affect and reduced anxiety during awake craniotomy.

reports.title: Seizure reduction via BRAF/Rest inhibition and neurogenesis ablation in epilepsy
reports.summary: These two papers study seizures in mouse models, examining vemurafenib and genetic inhibition of Rest (P1) and ablation of seizure-induced neurogenesis (P2). P1 reports a direct causal reduction of seizures by vemurafenib and by Rest inhibition, and its one matched press statement is aligned with the paper's strength. P2 reports no long-term seizure reduction from blocking post-status-epilepticus neurogenesis, with a transient effect only, and no press statement was matched to it. The two papers do not directly conflict, since they examine different interventions, but they point in different directions on whether targeting these pathways reduces seizures. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Vemurafenib, a BRAFV600E inhibitor, directly reduces seizures in mice.
Genetic inhibition of Rest reduces seizures in mice.
Blocking post-status-epilepticus neurogenesis shows no association with long-term seizure reduction, with only a transient effect over 10 days.

reports.title: Social factors, IL-6/STAT3 signaling, radiosurgery and hearing outcomes
reports.summary: This community covers hearing as the shared outcome, linked to social factors, IL-6/STAT3 signaling, and radiosurgery for vestibular schwannoma. Each of the three papers contributes one claim about a different exposure. The social-factors paper reports that social variables were associated with hearing, and the NF2 schwannoma paper reports that IL-6/STAT3 signaling was associated with decreased hearing function. The VISAS-K1 study found no association found between radiosurgery and hearing preservation versus observation, and the claims do not directly conflict because they examine different exposures. Only the VISAS-K1 claim had a press match, labeled aligned, while the other two claims had no press statement matched.

key_findings.text: Radiosurgery showed no association found with hearing preservation compared with observation in Koos grade I vestibular schwannoma, with no significant difference at 5 and 8 years.
IL-6/STAT3 signaling was associated with decreased hearing function in NF2 schwannoma rodent and patient data.
Social factors were associated with hearing, alongside vision and executive function, in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.

reports.title: Cortisol levels associated with acute myocardial infarction and dscaml1 deficiency
reports.summary: This community covers cortisol as a shared exposure, linked to acute myocardial infarction in one paper and to higher levels in dscaml1 mutant animals in another. Both claims are correlational in strength, and they point in the same direction (increase) without conflicting, though they come from different studies and test different links. The press label for the acute myocardial infarction claim is aligned with its paper. The dscaml1 claim has one overstated press statement (press strength 3 against paper strength 1) and one aligned press statement. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Elevated cortisol in the month before the event was associated with acute myocardial infarction in a case-control study of middle-aged persons.
dscaml1 mutant animals were associated with higher baseline cortisol levels and attenuated responses to acute stressors.

reports.title: Memory rehabilitation and hippocampal vascular supply effects on verbal learning
reports.summary: These findings study verbal learning in relation to two exposures: a modified story memory technique in traumatic brain injury and the vascular supply of the hippocampus. For the memory technique, no association was found with the CVLT-II learning slope after treatment, relative to placebo, after adjustment for education, baseline slope and PS performance. For hippocampal vascular supply, a mixed supply was associated with better verbal list learning and global cognition. The two papers point in opposite directions on verbal learning, but they study different exposures, so this is not a direct contradiction. Press coverage is recorded for only one claim: the hippocampal vascular supply finding, which press releases stated aligned with the paper's strength. The memory technique claim has no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: A modified story memory technique showed no association with the CVLT-II verbal learning slope after treatment, relative to placebo.
A mixed hippocampal vascular supply was associated with better verbal list learning and global cognition.
The verbal learning findings conflict in direction: a null result for the memory technique sits beside a positive association for hippocampal vascular supply.

reports.title: Cognitive processing speed and executive function across neurological conditions and interventions
reports.summary: The claims study cognitive outcomes such as processing speed, executive function, verbal knowledge and memory in stroke, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury, Parkinson disease, concussion, psychotic disorders and healthy adults, along with exercise, supplement and stimulation interventions. Aerobic exercise is the most strongly stated exposure, with one study describing it as facilitating processing speed and a systematic review reporting improved executive function, while most other associations are correlational. The papers conflict: aerobic fitness is linked to processing speed only in people with thalamic atrophy, and processing speed did not predict memory benefit from one rehabilitation program but did predict change after another treatment. Press coverage was mostly aligned with the paper wording across matched claims (21 aligned, 4 overstated, 1 understated), with overstatement noted for C5, C22, C28 and C40.

key_findings.text: Aerobic exercise is reported to facilitate processing speed in visual working memory and to improve executive function in a systematic review of Parkinson disease trials.
Aerobic fitness is associated with processing speed in people with multiple sclerosis who have thalamic atrophy, while no association was found in those without atrophy.
Reaction time and processing speed are associated with word-finding difficulty and executive function decline in older adults.
Processing speed did not predict memory benefit from learning rehabilitation in TBI, yet it predicted post-treatment change in another treatment trial.

Education and executive function show opposite patterns: college graduates had higher initial executive function after stroke, but a faster subsequent decline, and psychotic disorder is associated with lower verbal knowledge and executive function while methylphenidate increased psychotic disorder risk.

reports.title: Youth football tackling, Guardian Caps, age, and injury; antipsychotic use in children
reports.summary: This community pairs a youth football head-impact study with a study of antipsychotic prescribing in children, so the two papers share no exposure or outcome. The football paper links safe tackling technique, Guardian Caps, and age to decreased injury, worded as having possibly contributed to few impacts and no injuries. The antipsychotic paper reports antipsychotic agents associated with increased injury, with the effect noted among children with intellectual difficulty or autism. No findings agree or conflict across the two papers, and neither paper is retracted. For press coverage, the safe tackling finding was overstated (press 3 vs paper 2) in one matched statement and aligned in another, the Guardian Caps finding was aligned, the age finding had no press match, and the antipsychotic injury finding was overstated (press 2 vs paper 1) in one matched statement.

key_findings.text: Safe tackling technique, Guardian Caps, and the age of participants may have contributed to decreased injury in youth football head-impact data.
Antipsychotic agents are associated with increased injury, with the paper noting a higher rate of injury among children with intellectual difficulty or autism.

Press coverage overstated the safe tackling technique finding (press 3 vs paper 2) and the antipsychotic injury finding (press 2 vs paper 1), while the Guardian Caps finding was aligned with the paper.

reports.title: Diabetes effects on blood-brain barrier and antipsychotic-linked diabetes
reports.summary: These claims cover diabetes-related changes to brain capillary structure in one paper and an association between antipsychotic use and diabetes in another. The blood-brain barrier study reports that diabetes promotes tight junction involution, pericyte regression, and endothelial fenestration in hippocampal capillaries. The antipsychotic study reports only an association with diabetes, so the two papers neither directly agree nor conflict. Press coverage of the capillary finding was aligned with the paper, while press coverage of the antipsychotic association was aligned in one match and overstated in another.

key_findings.text: Diabetes promotes tight junction involution, pericyte regression, and endothelial fenestration in hippocampal capillaries.
Antipsychotic use is associated with diabetes in children.

reports.title: Education as an exposure across cognitive testing and moral judgment
reports.summary: Both claims in this community study education as an exposure, with one outcome being Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III scores and the other being moral judgment. The two findings come from unrelated papers, so they do not agree or conflict with each other. The ACE-III paper reports that education independently affects scores, with the direction unclear. The moral judgment paper reports no association between education and moral judgment. Neither claim has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Education was reported to independently affect Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III scores, with the direction of the effect unclear.
No association was found between education and moral judgment.

reports.title: Frailty, physical function, and nonpharmacological dementia interventions in older adults
reports.summary: The two papers study different exposures that share physical function as an outcome: a frailty score in one and nonpharmacological dementia interventions in the other. The frailty study reports that people in the highest frailty score group were associated with functional limitation, which is a correlational result. The dementia intervention trial found no association between the interventions and physical function over 12 weeks, so the two papers do not conflict directly. Press coverage was checked for only one claim: the null intervention finding was aligned with its press statement, and the frailty claim had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Participants in the highest frailty score group were associated with functional limitation and poorer physical function after adjustment.
No association was found between nonpharmacological interventions and physical function over the 12-week intervention period.

reports.title: Opioid analgesics linked to EEG changes and medication-related harm
reports.summary: This community covers opioid analgesics as the shared exposure, with two outcomes: EEG power and frequency, and medication-related harm. Two papers contribute three claims: P1, a multitaper spectrogram program for EEG data, reports associations between opioid analgesics and EEG power and frequency, while P2, a UK multicentre prospective study of older adults after hospital discharge, reports opioid analgesics among medicine classes associated with medication-related harm. The EEG claims are associational with unclear direction, and the P2 claim is associational with an increase in harm. The papers do not directly agree or conflict, since they study different outcomes and report no opposing directions for the same relationship. No press statements matched any claim, so press coverage cannot be compared, and no papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Opioid analgesics were associated with increased medication-related harm in older adults following hospital discharge.
Opioid analgesics were associated with EEG power, with the direction of effect unclear.
Opioid analgesics were associated with EEG frequency, with the direction of effect unclear.

reports.title: Microglia and amyloid plaques, myelin phagocytosis, and ischemic brain injury
reports.summary: These findings study microglia in relation to three outcomes: amyloid plaque formation, myelin phagocytosis, and brain ischemia. The Alzheimer's model study reports a direct causal link between microglia and plaque formation, which is the strongest wording in the community. The myelin study reports microglia associated with myelin phagocytosis, and the stroke study describes microglia in ischemic brain injury with tentative 'may' language about new therapeutic avenues. No papers report opposing directions, so there is no direct conflict among these findings. Only the myelin claim has a press match, and its press statement is aligned with the paper's strength; the plaque and stroke claims have no press coverage matched to them.

key_findings.text: Microglia are reported to increase amyloid plaque formation, with the paper stating microglia play roles in initiating plaque pathogenesis.
Microglia are associated with increased myelin phagocytosis in developmental myelination.
Microglia are reported to participate in ischemic brain injury, though the stroke paper uses tentative wording and its direction is unclear.

reports.title: Opioid, PI3K/Akt, MEK/ERK, and CREB signaling in fear extinction
reports.summary: The two papers study how δ-opioid receptor signaling, MEK/ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways, and CREB expression relate to fear extinction. P1 reports that δ-opioid receptor activity may increase fear extinction, and that the KNT-127 effect may be mediated by MEK/ERK signaling in the BLA and PI3K/Akt signaling in the IL. P2 reports that extinction is associated with reduced CREB expression and that increased CREB expression inhibits extinction, and it states that CREB may function as a molecular switch regulating fear and its extinction. Press coverage aligned with the paper's strength for the MEK/ERK and PI3K/Akt claims but overstated the δ-opioid association, with press stating it at strength 2 against a paper strength of 1. The CREB claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: The δ-opioid receptor may increase fear extinction, according to P1.
P1 links the δ-opioid receptor to fear extinction only as associated with it, yet press coverage stated the link more strongly than the paper did.
P1 suggests the KNT-127 effect may be mediated by PI3K/Akt signaling in the IL and MEK/ERK signaling in the BLA, and press coverage aligned with both pathway claims.
P2 reports that extinction is associated with reduced CREB expression, and that increased CREB expression inhibits extinction.
P2 states that CREB may function as a molecular switch regulating fear and its extinction, with the direction of effect unclear.

reports.title: Pembrolizumab and selumetinib tumor response in meningioma and neurofibroma
reports.summary: The two papers study tumor response to pembrolizumab in recurrent or residual high-grade meningiomas and to selumetinib in inoperable plexiform neurofibromas. Both report an increase in tumor response, so the findings do not conflict. The pembrolizumab claim is conditional (strength 2, "may"), while the selumetinib claim is correlational (strength 1, "associated with"). Press releases overstated both findings relative to the strength of the papers' wording. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Pembrolizumab may increase tumor response in a subset of recurrent and residual high-grade meningiomas.
Selumetinib is associated with increased tumor response in children with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas.
Press releases overstated both the pembrolizumab and the selumetinib findings relative to the papers' wording.

reports.title: Treatments associated with decreased tumor volume in glioblastoma and neurofibroma
reports.summary: This community groups two findings that study treatments and tumor volume: optical blood-brain-tumor barrier modulation (optobbtb) in glioblastoma, and selumetinib in children with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas. Both papers report a decrease in tumor volume, so the findings do not conflict in direction. The glioblastoma paper (P1) states that optobbtb treatment reduces tumor volume, and its press coverage is aligned with the paper's wording. The selumetinib trial (P2) reports only an association with tumor shrinkage, and no press statement was matched to it. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Optobbtb treatment reduces tumor volume in glioblastoma, with press coverage aligned with the paper's statement.
Selumetinib is associated with tumor shrinkage in children with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas, and no press statement was matched to this finding.

reports.title: Neuronal activation linked to punishment and food-seeking learning
reports.summary: This community groups two studies of learning-related exposures and increased neuronal activation. Paper P1 reports that punishment is associated with increased activation of parvalbumin-expressing basal forebrain neurons. Paper P2 reports that food self-administration learning is associated with greater Fos-measured activation in the medial prefrontal cortex, with learners also showing more food-seeking than non-learners. The two papers study different exposures and brain regions, so they neither agree nor conflict directly. No press statements matched either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Punishment is associated with increased neuronal activation in parvalbumin-expressing basal forebrain neurons.
Food self-administration learning is associated with increased neuronal activation within the medial prefrontal cortex, alongside greater food-seeking behavior in learners than in non-learners.

reports.title: Music reward, movie genres, genetics, and brain reward-region correlates
reports.summary: These claims study music reward sensitivity, nucleus accumbens activity and white matter connectivity, genetic influences on music enjoyment and drug condemnation, movie genre preferences, and telomere length with brain volume. Papers agree that the nucleus accumbens and its connections are associated with music reward sensitivity, and that genetic factors contribute to it. The findings conflict on the nucleus accumbens response to movie genres, where comedy preference is linked to increased activity while crime/thriller and documentary preference are linked to decreased activity. Of the 18 claims, 7 matched a press statement: six were aligned with the paper, and one (C5, on genetic influences on music reward) was overstated.

key_findings.text: Nucleus accumbens activity and its tract connectivity are associated with music reward sensitivity.
Diffusivity measures in orbitofrontal white matter tracts are inversely associated with music reward sensitivity.
Genetic effects contribute up to 54% of the variability in music reward sensitivity, partly distinct from music perceptual ability, though one press release overstated the genetic influence.
Comedy genre preference is associated with increased nucleus accumbens activity, while crime/thriller and documentary preferences are associated with decreased activity.
Shorter leucocyte telomere length is associated with smaller accumbens volume.

reports.title: Visual features and pop-out effects on visual search efficiency
reports.summary: The findings study how visual features such as color, motion, size and orientation, along with distractor suppression, affect visual search efficiency. Paper P1 reports that all four features facilitate efficient search in archerfish, comparable to humans, and paper P2 reports in monkeys that visual cortex inverts an attentional capture signal into suppression to aid search. The claims do not conflict, since each reports a direct increase in search efficiency. Four of the five claims are matched by press releases with aligned strength, so press coverage matches the papers' wording. The distractor suppression claim from P2 has no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Color, motion, size and orientation each directly increase visual search efficiency in archerfish, comparable to humans.
In monkey visual cortex, distractor suppression directly increases visual search by inverting an attentional capture signal.

reports.title: Autoantibodies, 2-deoxyglucose, and excitatory synaptic activity in brain disorders
reports.summary: The two claims study whether anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies alter excitatory synaptic transmission in mice and whether 2-deoxyglucose alters excitatory synaptic activity after traumatic brain injury. The papers examine different exposures and do not overlap in their outcomes, so no agreement or conflict between them can be assessed. Paper P1 reports a direct causal decrease in miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency, and paper P2 reports a direct causal increase in excitatory synaptic activity. The one claim with a press match (C2) was labeled aligned, and the other claim (C1) had no press statement matched to it. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies reduced the frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents in mouse frontal cortex.
In a traumatic brain injury model, one week of 2-deoxyglucose treatment restored excitatory and inhibitory synaptic activity.

reports.title: Stress, depression, ADHD, brain injury and dementia-related exposures and outcomes
reports.summary: The claims cover stress and depression, ADHD, traumatic brain injury, smoking, infection, dietary and blood biomarkers, and their links to dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and related outcomes. Most relationships are described as associations (strength 1), while a few are stated directly, such as ADHD slowing speech processing and branched-chain amino acids reducing concussion symptoms in a pilot trial. Papers conflict in places: one study reports infection linked to Alzheimer's disease only in early-onset cases and no association at age 60 or older, while another claim from the same paper states an increase, and a cohort reports no association between occupational physical activity and dementia alongside a positive result for mild cognitive impairment. Press coverage of the matched claims is mostly aligned with the papers, with chronic stress and cardiac events and vital exhaustion and dementia labelled overstated, and the ADHD speech-processing finding labelled understated. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Chronic stress and depression were associated with higher odds of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease in one cohort.
ADHD was stated to slow speech processing in adverse listening conditions and to increase hesitation, though press coverage understated this finding.
No association was found between traumatic brain injury and beta-amyloid or glucose metabolism in veterans.
Infection was linked to Alzheimer's disease only in cases diagnosed before 60, with no association found at 60 or older, so the same paper's findings conflict in direction across claims.
Higher phosphatidylcholine intake and longer leucocyte telomere length were each associated with a lower risk of dementia or Alzheimer's disease, and press coverage matched these as aligned.

reports.title: Five unrelated papers: diverse exposures and outcomes, no shared theme
reports.summary: This community groups five papers on unrelated topics, including autism polygenic scores, COVID-19 iron dysregulation, nonpharmacological dementia interventions, post-exertional malaise, and pediatric vestibular schwannomas, with outcomes such as suicidal ideation, persistent symptoms, and mass effect. The findings do not converge on a shared relationship. Four claims report increases, three at associational strength and one (C2) phrased as 'may' contribute. The only null result (C3) reports no association found between nonpharmacological interventions and behavioral symptoms. Press coverage matched only two claims: C2 and C5 were aligned with their papers, and the other three had no press match. None of the papers are retracted.

key_findings.text: Defects in iron homeostasis may contribute to persisting symptoms after COVID-19, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
Depressive symptoms are associated with suicidal behaviour and ideation in people with autism polygenic scores.
Pediatric age is associated with symptoms of mass effect in vestibular schwannomas, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
A history of post-exertional malaise is associated with more objective signs of disease in post-COVID-19 syndrome.
No association found between nonpharmacological interventions and behavioral symptoms in community-dwelling older adults with dementia.

reports.title: Pupil response associations with neuronal noise, integration kernel, and head impacts
reports.summary: These findings study pupil response as the outcome, examined in relation to neuronal noise and the integration kernel in one paper and to high-acceleration head impacts in another. The first paper reports that pupil response is associated with neuronal noise and the integration kernel, with individual differences tied to the kernel and trial-by-trial fluctuations tied to noise. The second paper reports that measurable changes in pupil response were found after clinically asymptomatic head impacts in high school football athletes. All five claims are correlational (strength 1) with unclear direction, so no claims point in opposite directions. Both claims from the first paper were matched by press statements labelled aligned, while the head-impact claim had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Pupil response is associated with neuronal noise, with trial-by-trial fluctuations in pupil response associated with trial-by-trial fluctuations in noise.
Pupil response is associated with the integration kernel, with individual differences in pupil response associated with individual differences in the integration kernel.
Measurable changes in pupil response are associated with high-acceleration head impacts in high school football athletes, though no press coverage was matched to this finding.

reports.title: Neural replay and consolidation in skill, stress, threat, and BCI studies
reports.summary: This community covers neural replay and memory-related brain processes across four papers: skill consolidation, stress, aversive memory, and brain-computer interface adaptation. Replay is the shared thread between P1 and P3, which link it to skill consolidation and to stress-related decreases, respectively, while P2 and P4 study separate exposures and outcomes. Press coverage overstated the strength of C1 and C3, although C1 also had an aligned press match, while C2 and C5 were aligned with their papers. C4 had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Hippocampo-neocortical replay increases skill consolidation, according to P1.
Replay selective for the trained sequence is associated with the magnitude of skill consolidation in P1.
Psychological stress is associated with decreased neural replay in P3, and press coverage overstated this finding.
CGRP-expressing neurons increase aversive memory formation, according to P2.
Long-term closed-loop decoder adaptation increases neural map consolidation in P4, with no matched press statement.

reports.title: Synapse number changes linked to Fn14, visual experience, and NRXN1α autoantibodies
reports.summary: These claims study synapse number and spine density, covering Fn14 signalling and visual experience in one Neuron paper and NRXN1α autoantibodies in one Brain Behavior and Immunity paper. The two papers study different exposures and point in opposite directions: Fn14 is reported to increase synapse number, while anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies are reported to reduce spine and synapse density. The effect of visual experience on synapse number is described only as altering it, with the direction unclear, and the Fn14 link to bulbous spine-associated synapses is stated more cautiously as possibly increasing them. Press coverage matched the Fn14 synapse-number claim and the NRXN1α claim, both labelled aligned, while the visual experience and bulbous spine claims had no press match. Neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Fn14 is reported to increase synapse number, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
Administration of anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies is reported to reduce spine and synapse density in the frontal cortex, with press coverage aligned with the paper.
Fn14 may increase bulbous spine-associated synapses at retinogeniculate connections.
Visual experience alters the number and structure of retinogeniculate synapses, with the direction of change unclear.

reports.title: Interneuron ablation and microglial TWEAK signaling reduce dendritic spines
reports.summary: The two findings study different exposures: ablation of dentate hilar somatostatin-positive interneurons and TWEAK signaling from microglia, each linked to decreased spine measures. Both papers use direct causal wording (strength 3) and report decreases, so they do not conflict. Only the TWEAK finding (C2) has a matched press statement, and it is labeled aligned with the paper. The interneuron finding (C1) has no matched press statement. No retracted papers are in this community.

key_findings.text: Ablating hilar somatostatin-positive interneurons reduces dendritic spine density in the dentate gyrus.
TWEAK signaling from microglia reduces bulbous spines on relay neurons at retinogeniculate connections, leading to elimination of a subset of connections.

reports.title: Hippocampal memory circuits and dopamine neuron loss in neurodegeneration models
reports.summary: These ten papers study hippocampal memory circuits, dopaminergic neurons, and models of Parkinson's disease and schizophrenia, with exposures such as VGLUT expression, parvalbumin interneuron excitability, perineuronal nets, TFE3, and male sex. Within the community, parvalbumin interneuron findings in CA1 agree with each other, and the two VGLUT claims from one Aging Cell paper agree on sex-linked dopamine neuron loss. Direction conflicts are limited: the evaluative-signal paper reports no effect on dopamine responses to aversive stimuli (C3) while reporting an increase in responses to reward (C13), and the memory-signal study reports only an unclear, weakly stated link to dopaminergic activity (C5). Press coverage matched 10 claims: 7 were aligned, 4 understated and 3 overstated, and no retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Restoring parvalbumin interneuron excitability in a schizophrenia mouse model restored wild-type-like CA1 network dynamics and hippocampal-dependent behaviour in adulthood.
Assembly of perineuronal nets and maturation of parvalbumin interneurons are necessary and sufficient for competitive engram allocation and memory precision in the developing hippocampus.
Males showed significantly greater age-related dopamine neuron loss and locomotor decline than females, and diminishing VGLUT expression in dopamine neurons eliminated females' greater resilience.
VGLUT expression regulation is essential for dopamine neuron survival in aging mice, though the paper frames its role as a potential compensatory mechanism.
TFE3 overexpression mitigated dopaminergic neuron loss and restored motor function in an α-synuclein model of Parkinson's disease.

reports.title: Psychosocial stress, locus of control, and stroke outcomes across studies
reports.summary: These findings study psychosocial stress, locus of control, and life events as exposures linked to stroke, alongside stroke mortality trends and COVID-19-related stroke. The strongest evidence comes from one paper reporting that stress at home, stress at work, and recent stressful life events were each associated with higher odds of acute stroke. A second paper reports that higher locus of control was associated with lower odds of stroke and weakened the stress associations. Other papers describe stroke mortality rising with age and declining faster for ischaemic than haemorrhagic stroke, and a COVID-19 series noting cardiovascular risk factors among patients with stroke. Press coverage aligned with the paper strength in six matched claims, while one press statement on psychosocial stress overstated the association; the COVID-19 and mortality claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: Psychosocial stress was associated with an increased risk of acute stroke.
Recent stressful life events were associated with an increased risk of acute stroke.
Higher locus of control was associated with reduced odds of stroke and diminished the association between stress and acute stroke.
Stroke mortality increased sharply with advancing age.
Stroke mortality declined more steeply for ischaemic than haemorrhagic strokes.

reports.title: Medial temporal lobe activity linked to prosocial intentions and perceptual change
reports.summary: The community groups two studies that link medial temporal lobe (MTL) activity to different outcomes: prosocial intentions and perceptual change. Both claims are correlational (strength 1), so neither paper asserts a causal relationship. The prosociality paper reports MTL activity associated with the effect of conditions on prosocial intentions, and an increase in that effect that remained when right temporoparietal junction activity was disrupted. The perception paper reports medial temporal lobe neuron activity associated with perceptual change, and its one press-matched statement is labelled aligned. The other two claims have no press match, so press coverage can only be compared for that single case.

key_findings.text: Medial temporal lobe neuron activity is associated with perceptual change, preceding it by about 1000 ms.
MTL activity is associated with the effect of conditions on prosocial intentions.
The association of MTL activity with prosocial intentions remained when right temporoparietal junction activity was disrupted.

reports.title: Stress, sleep, hippocampal plasticity, memory encoding and sexual function
reports.summary: This community groups 34 claims from 15 papers on stress, sleep, hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP), memory encoding, and sexual function, and 14 of these claims have a matched press statement. Stress is linked to worse sexual function in one human study, while several mouse and human studies link stress, exercise, and sleep to LTP, memory, or performance, mostly at strength 1 ('associated with'). The papers conflict on GLDC copy number and LTP, and on whether potentiation 24 hours after pairing produces lasting memory, because the same paper's claims are coded with opposite or null results. Among matched claims, press labels are 6 overstated, 6 aligned, and 3 understated, and the overstated cases are mostly sleep and memory papers where press strength was 3 against paper strength 1 or 2. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Stress is associated with worse sexual functioning and lower sexual satisfaction in young men who have sex with men.
In mice, stress reduced dorsal CA1 LTP while exercise increased LTP.
A GLDC triplication in mice suppresses LTP in dentate gyrus synapses, but another claim from the same paper records no effect on LTP with the same wording.
NREM sleep is associated with improved behavioral performance and with restorative effects in human studies.
In mice, potentiation minutes after pairing produced lasting memory, while the 24-hour result is recorded both as producing memory and as producing none.

reports.title: Caffeine intake, neuronal cytoarchitecture, HDAC6 inhibition and migraine
reports.summary: These findings study migraine in relation to caffeinated beverage intake, neuronal cytoarchitecture, and HDAC6 inhibition. One prospective cohort reports a statistically significant nonlinear association between caffeinated beverage intake and migraine headache occurrence on the same day, but individual intake levels were not significant. That same paper's wording suggests high intake may trigger migraine, which press coverage described more weakly than the paper. A preclinical study reports that neuronal cytoarchitecture disruptions are a feature of chronic migraine and associates them with migraine, and press coverage matched that strength. The same preclinical study links HDAC6 inhibition with decreased migraine outcomes, a finding with no press match. No papers in this community report conflicting directions.

key_findings.text: Caffeinated beverage intake is associated with migraine headache occurrence on the same day, with a significant nonlinear trend but no significant estimates at individual intake levels.
High caffeinated beverage intake may trigger migraine headaches on that day, a conditional statement that press coverage understated.
