Disruptions in neuronal cytoarchitecture are associated with chronic migraine, and press coverage stated this with matching strength.
HDAC6 inhibition is associated with decreased migraine in validated mouse models, a finding with no matched press coverage.

reports.title: Attention outcomes across neural correlations, Lewy body pathology, and noradrenergic treatment
reports.summary: This community groups three findings that share attention as an exposure or outcome, drawn from neural-correlation, Lewy body pathology, and noradrenergic treatment studies. Lewy body pathology was associated with worse attention in cognitively impaired individuals, and attention was associated with a decrease in mean pairwise correlation in macaque V4 population recordings. A systematic review and meta-analysis found no association between noradrenergic drugs and attention in Alzheimer's disease. The papers do not study the same exposure-outcome pair, but the null noradrenergic result sits beside the positive Lewy body result on attention. None of these claims has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared with them.

key_findings.text: Lewy body pathology was associated with worse attention, executive, visuospatial and motor function in cognitively impaired individuals, independent of amyloid-β or tau.
No association was found between noradrenergic drugs and attention in Alzheimer's disease in a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Attention was associated with a decrease in mean pairwise correlation in macaque V4 population recordings, which the paper attributes to three distinct changes in population-wide covariability.

reports.title: Hemorrhage as exposure: collaterals in stroke and nursing home admissions
reports.summary: This community groups two papers that share only the term hemorrhage, one on stroke reperfusion and one on nursing facility resident transfers. P1 reports in mice that leptomeningeal collaterals reduce hemorrhage after recanalization, and press coverage of this claim was aligned with the paper's strength. P2 reports that hematological or bleeding diagnoses are associated with lower odds of hospital admission among long-stay nursing facility residents, and no press statement was matched to this claim. The two papers study different populations and do not agree or conflict with each other. Neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: In mice, leptomeningeal collaterals reduce hemorrhage after recanalization.
Nursing facility residents with hematological or bleeding diagnoses are associated with lower odds of hospital admission.

reports.title: Stroke recovery: reperfusion, collaterals, and RXRα-linked brain cleanup
reports.summary: These two claims concern factors that affect functional recovery after ischemic stroke: reperfusion in patients with poor leptomeningeal collaterals, and RXRα deficiency in myeloid phagocytes in mice. The Neuron study (P1) reports that rapid reperfusion decreases functional recovery in thrombectomy patients with poor collaterals (C1). The Stroke paper (P2) reports only an association between RXRα deficiency and worse late recovery and larger brain atrophy in mice (C2). The two findings address different exposures and do not conflict, and both report decreased recovery. Press coverage of C1 was mixed, with one press statement understating the paper's strength and another matching it. The press coverage of C2 aligned with the paper's wording. Neither paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Rapid reperfusion decreased functional recovery in stroke patients with poor leptomeningeal collaterals undergoing thrombectomy.
RXRα deficiency in myeloid phagocytes was associated with worse late functional recovery and larger brain atrophy in mice.

reports.title: Lewy body dementia links to drawing measures and α-synuclein PET uptake
reports.summary: This community covers Lewy body dementia, linked to drawing-process measures in one paper and to α-synuclein PET tracer uptake in another. The drawing study (P1) reports that LBD was associated with reduced speed and smoothness, while increased pauses and total durations were seen in both the AD and LBD groups. The imaging study (P2) reports that PET signal from 18F-C05-05 was associated with increased uptake in the midbrains of PD and DLB patients compared with healthy controls. All five claims use correlational wording, and no papers report opposite directions or null results. Press coverage matched only the PET finding (C2), which was aligned with the paper; no press statements were matched to the drawing findings.

key_findings.text: Lewy body dementia was associated with reduced drawing speed and smoothness, along with increased pauses and total drawing duration.
PET-detectable 18F-C05-05 signal was associated with increased uptake in the midbrains of PD and DLB patients compared with healthy controls, and press coverage of this finding was aligned.

reports.title: Deprescribing and pharmacist interventions for medication burden and adverse drug events
reports.summary: These claims cover deprescribing and pharmacist-led interventions in older adults, with outcomes of medication burden, adverse drug events (ADEs), and deprescribing decisions. The deprescribing trial (P1) reports reduced medication burden, potentially inappropriate medication exposure, and medication count, but no difference in ADE rates. The pharmacist-led systematic review (P3) reports that 43% of studies found significant ADE reductions and 56% found no effect, and it frames its conclusion as a potential benefit. Press coverage was mostly aligned with paper strength, but two claims were overstated: C6 for the pharmacist review and C10 for the medication count result. The LLM study (P2) found no effect of ADL status in binary deprescribing decisions (C2) but a linear increase in deprescribing with greater ADL impairment (C11), so the two claims conflict.

key_findings.text: The deprescribing trial reported that the intervention reduced total medication burden and Drug Burden Index, and reduced exposure to potentially inappropriate medications.
The deprescribing trial found no difference in adverse drug event rates between intervention and control groups.
Pharmacist-led interventions were reported to reduce adverse drug events in 43% of studies, while 56% showed no effect, and the review suggests they have potential to reduce ADEs.
The deprescribing trial reported that intervention patients took 14% to 15% fewer medications than controls, a result press coverage stated more strongly than the paper.
In the LLM study, ADL impairment was associated with more deprescribing, while ADL status showed no effect in binary deprescribing decisions.

reports.title: COVID-19 symptoms, neurological markers, and autonomic and cognitive outcomes
reports.summary: The findings study COVID-19 against symptoms, brain and glial biomarkers, autonomic nerve activity, dementia, and well-being, alongside several mechanistic papers on unrelated exposures such as ependymal de-differentiation, paraquat, and vagotomy. Papers agree that COVID-19 is associated with raised glial and neuronal injury markers and with increased muscle sympathetic nerve activity, though these are correlational findings (strength 1). Conflicts appear in well-being, where social participation improved but other well-being domains showed no difference, and in blood pressure, where no differences were found. Press coverage was aligned for 22 matched claims and overstated for 10, including the obesity, hair loss, fatigue, neocortical dysfunction, and Alzheimer's claims, and the null well-being result (C40). Two mechanistic papers (C4, C12) use direct causal wording, and press coverage of C12 was understated in one statement.

key_findings.text: COVID-19 is associated with raised glial and neuronal injury markers in blood or cerebrospinal fluid.
COVID-19 is associated with higher resting muscle sympathetic nerve burst frequency than controls.

Compared with common respiratory infections, SARS-CoV-2 is associated with post-infection fatigue, dyspnea, and other symptoms, while dyspnea declined over 30 days but stayed above negative-test levels.
Well-being improved in COVID-19-positive participants only for social participation, with no difference in other well-being domains.
SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia is associated with higher odds of new-onset dementia than pneumonia unrelated to SARS-CoV-2 (OR 1.3).

reports.title: Education, noradrenergic drugs, and protein misfolding in global cognition
reports.summary: The claims study how education, noradrenergic drugs, quadruple misfolded proteins, and hippocampal vascular supply relate to global cognition. A meta-analysis reports that noradrenergic drugs improved global cognition, and the same review says they may offer effective treatment for general cognition in Alzheimer disease. Education was associated with higher initial global cognition after stroke, while a separate claim found no association with declines in global cognition or memory. Quadruple misfolded proteins were associated with lower global cognition, and a mixed hippocampal vascular supply with higher global cognition. Press coverage matched four claims, all labelled aligned, and the two unmatched claims are C3 and C5.

key_findings.text: Noradrenergic drugs improved global cognition in Alzheimer disease in a meta-analysis of 10 studies with 1300 patients.
The same review states that noradrenergic drugs may offer effective treatment for general cognition in Alzheimer disease.
Higher education was associated with better initial global cognition after stroke, but education was not associated with declines in global cognition or memory.
Quadruple misfolded proteins were associated with lower global cognition, with the lowest final MMSE scores in that group.
A mixed hippocampal vascular supply was associated with better global cognition and verbal list learning.

reports.title: Cognitive performance associations with diet, biomarkers, social factors, and therapies
reports.summary: The seven papers study links between cognitive performance and dietary choline, blood and CSF biomarkers, parental education and brain connectivity, acculturation, exercise-related biomarkers, and an experimental compound in mouse models. Most relationships are reported as correlational (strength 1), and the mouse study reports a stronger, direct improvement in cognition. No findings conflict in direction, although the parental education finding is unclear in direction. Press coverage was labeled aligned for five claims, while the mouse study's press statement was understated relative to the paper, and three claims had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Dietary choline and phosphatidylcholine intakes were associated with better performance on cognitive tests of frontal and temporal lobe function.
In mouse models of Alzheimer disease, the compound A11 ameliorated neuroinflammation and improved cognitive performance.
A longitudinal rise in plasma neurofilament light correlated with poor cognitive performance in patients with Alzheimer disease.
Cerebrospinal fluid DOPA decarboxylase levels were associated with worse cognitive performance in the study population.
Low acculturation was associated with poorer cognitive performance among older Hispanics.

reports.title: Neurodegeneration biomarkers and early neuronal dysfunction across Alzheimer's and Parkinson's studies
reports.summary: The community covers neurodegeneration as an outcome, linked to plasma neurofilament light, early neuronal dysfunction, PU.1 binding, and SQSTM1 across four papers. Plasma NfL is associated with neurodegeneration in Alzheimer disease patients, and the paper suggests it may be useful as a noninvasive biomarker. In Parkinson disease patient-specific neuronal networks, early neuronal dysfunction may contribute to degenerative pathways before dopaminergic neuron loss. No claims report opposite directions, but the direction of the SQSTM1 association with neurodegeneration is unclear. Only the mouse PU.1 binding claim has a press match, and that press statement is aligned with the paper; the other three claims have no press statement.

key_findings.text: Plasma neurofilament light is associated with neurodegeneration in patients with Alzheimer disease.
Early neuronal dysfunction may contribute to the initiation of degenerative pathways preceding dopaminergic neuron loss in Parkinson disease.
In transgenic mice with neurodegeneration, PU.1 binding was associated with increased levels, and press coverage of this finding was aligned with the paper.
SQSTM1 showed a significant association with neurodegeneration after adjustment for age, sex, and APOE ε4 genotype, with direction unclear.

reports.title: Brain functional connectivity across substance use, dissociation, sleep, and dementia studies
reports.summary: These findings mostly study functional connectivity in brain networks, especially the default mode network, in relation to exposures such as cannabis and nicotine use, dissociation, sleep disturbance, polygenic risk, and body movement. The papers agree that connectivity is associated with several conditions, but they conflict on direction: body movement is reported to decrease default mode network activity while facial movement is reported to increase BOLD signal, and p factor is linked to hyperconnectivity while pathology is linked to decreased connectivity. A null result for combined cannabis and nicotine use sits beside positive associations for the same networks. Press coverage was mostly aligned with the papers, with four claims overstated and one understated. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Cannabis and nicotine use were associated with functional connectivity in resting state networks, with a post-hoc comparison finding no association found between CTRL and NIC+CAN users.
Sleep disturbance was associated with reduced connectivity in default mode network regions, and default mode network structure and function underpins sleep problems after pediatric concussion.
Dissociation and its subtypes were associated with altered connectivity in the central executive, default, and salience networks.
Body movement was reported to deactivate default mode network nodes, whereas facial movement was reported to produce a positive BOLD pattern, so the two studies point in opposite directions.

The p factor was associated with hyperconnectivity between visual and frontoparietal and default mode networks, while another study reported connectivity disruption across pathologies, a conflicting direction.

reports.title: Brain structure links to dementia risk, placebo response, and inhibitory control
reports.summary: These findings examine how brain structure relates to several outcomes: neighborhood disadvantage and dementia-related brain deficits, brain structure and placebo pill response in chronic back pain, and cognitive control network structure and inhibitory control in preschool children. Each relationship is reported as an association (strength 1), so none is stated as causal. The findings do not conflict with one another because they address different populations and outcomes. Press coverage matched two of the three claims, and both were labeled aligned with the paper's wording. The placebo claim had no matched press statement. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with dementia-related brain structural deficits and elevated dementia-risk scores.
Cortical and subcortical structure of the cognitive control network is associated with early inhibitory control in preschool children.
The response to placebo analgesic pills is associated with brain structure and function in chronic back pain patients.

reports.title: Attention-related modulation, judgment errors, and syntactic alignment in visual attention
reports.summary: These findings concern attention as an outcome of several exposures: microsaccades in the superior colliculus, the distribution of attention in judgments of group proportions, and syntactic alignment during speech planning. The microsaccade paper P1 reports both a null result (C1, no association found) and a weaker association when microsaccades were directed toward the cued location (C4, associated with), so its findings partly conflict. P2 and P3 each report a direct causal claim (C2, C3) with no matched press statement. Press coverage matched only the two P1 claims, and both were labeled aligned with the paper's wording. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Syntactic alignment in sentence planning induces more visual attention to agents than nonaligned planning.
Biased attention distribution underlies typical judgment errors about group proportions.
Microsaccades are not associated with attention-related modulation in the superior colliculus, since modulation appeared without them.
Attention-related modulation was still associated with microsaccades directed toward the cued location, which conflicts with the null result for microsaccades overall.

reports.title: SRT2104 SIRT1 activation and musical anhedonia outcomes
reports.summary: These two papers study unrelated exposures: one examines SRT2104, a SIRT1 activator, and anhedonia in mice, while the other examines musical anhedonia and groove response in people. Because the exposures and outcomes differ, the findings do not directly agree or conflict. The mouse study reports a direct causal reduction of anhedonia by SRT2104 (strength 3), with no press coverage matched to it. The human study reports no association between musical anhedonia and groove response (strength 0), and its press statement was aligned with the paper. Press coverage was matched for only one of the two claims, so no comparison across the community is possible.

key_findings.text: SRT2104, a SIRT1 activator, is reported to reverse chronic stress-induced anhedonia and behavioral despair in wild-type mice.
No association was found between musical anhedonia and groove response in a matched comparison of 17 people per group.

reports.title: Hippocampal place coding linked to subiculum projections and taste responses
reports.summary: The two papers study hippocampal place coding, one examining CA1-projecting subiculum neurons and their role in object-location learning, the other examining how taste responses interact with place fields in the hippocampus. The subiculum paper (C1) reports a projection that modulates place-specific CA1 activity, stated with direct causal wording but with an unclear direction in the claim. The taste paper (C2) reports that taste-responsive cells tend to have less spatially specific fields, which is an associational finding. The claims do not address the same exposure, so no agreement or conflict between the papers can be established. Press coverage matched only the taste paper, where the press statement was aligned with the paper's strength; the subiculum paper had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: CA1-projecting subicular neurons are reported to modulate place-specific firing of CA1 neurons, though the direction of this effect is unclear.
Taste-responsive cells are associated with less spatially specific firing fields, and place cells respond only to tastes delivered inside their place field.

reports.title: Motor neuron survival and innervation after SYT13 overexpression and BDNF hydrogel delivery
reports.summary: This community covers two papers on motor neuron health: one on synaptotagmin 13 (SYT13) and motor neuron survival in ALS and SMA patient cells, and one on local BDNF hydrogel delivery and diaphragm innervation by phrenic motor neurons after cervical spinal cord injury. Both papers state their relationships with direct causal wording, and they examine different exposures and outcomes, so they do not conflict. The SYT13 finding is the only one with a press match, and its press statement is labeled aligned with the paper's strength. The BDNF finding had no matched press statement, so press coverage of it cannot be compared. No papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: SYT13 overexpression improves survival and increases axon lengths of ALS and SMA patient motor neurons in vitro.
BDNF hydrogel delivery to the injured cervical spinal cord significantly preserved diaphragm innervation by phrenic motor neurons.

reports.title: Frontal and medial temporal neural activity linked to moral and perceptual responses
reports.summary: This community covers two unrelated neuroimaging studies: pIFC activity while witnessing others in pain and moral response tendencies, and medial frontal and medial temporal neuron activity preceding perceptual change. In P1, pIFC activity was associated with deontological response tendencies, and no association was found with utilitarian response tendencies. P2 reports medial frontal activity associated with perceptual change, with the direction of the relationship unclear. The two papers study different outcomes, so their findings do not directly conflict. Press coverage was aligned with the paper's strength for both P1 claims, and the P2 claim had no matched press statement.

key_findings.text: Activity in the posterior inferior frontal cortex while witnessing others in pain is associated with deontological response tendencies.
No association was found between posterior inferior frontal cortex activity and utilitarian response tendencies.
Medial frontal activity is associated with changes in the content of perception, with the direction of the effect unclear.

reports.title: Exposures and axonal mitochondrial transport in Parkinson's and FUS-ALS models
reports.summary: These findings study how environmental toxicants and neurodegeneration-linked factors affect axonal mitochondrial and lysosomal transport in neuronal models. Paper P1 reports that maneb, paraquat, rotenone and agrochemical exposure each decrease anterograde mitochondrial transport in SNCA-A53T stem cell neurons via nitration of α-tubulin. Paper P2 reports that magnetic stimulation increases axonal transport of mitochondria and lysosomes in FUS-ALS motoneurons. Paper P3 reports that paraquat increases oxidative stress in vagal neurons, but it does not address transport directly. Press coverage is matched for only two claims, both aligned with their papers, and the remaining claims have no press statement.

key_findings.text: Exposure to agrochemicals, rotenone, paraquat or maneb decreases anterograde mitochondrial transport in SNCA-A53T patient-derived neurons, via nitration of α-tubulin.
Magnetic stimulation increases axonal transport of mitochondria and lysosomes in cultured FUS-ALS motoneurons.
Paraquat is linked to increased oxidative stress in vagal neurons expressing α-synuclein, though the association is weaker.

reports.title: Aging, semantic interference, word-finding difficulty, and blueberry memory interference
reports.summary: This community covers two unrelated topics: age and semantic interference in word-finding difficulty (P1), and blueberry supplementation and memory interference in midlife (P2). The papers do not address the same exposures or outcomes, so there is no direct agreement or conflict between them. P1 reports that age is associated with increased semantic interference, but found no association between semantic interference and word-finding difficulty in connected speech. P2 reports that blueberry supplementation is associated with reduced memory interference. No press statements were matched to any claim, so press coverage cannot be compared, and no retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Age is associated with increased semantic interference across the lifespan.
No association was found between semantic interference and word-finding difficulty in connected speech.
Blueberry supplementation is associated with reduced memory interference.

reports.title: Xenon and blueberry supplementation effects on memory outcomes
reports.summary: The two claims study whether xenon treatment after traumatic brain injury and blueberry supplementation in midlife affect memory-related outcomes. Xenon is reported with a direct causal verb to prevent very late-onset TBI-related memory deficits in mice, while blueberry supplementation is only associated with reduced memory encoding difficulty in people. The papers study different exposures and populations, so they neither agree nor conflict directly. No press statements were matched to either claim, so press coverage cannot be compared.

key_findings.text: Xenon treatment was reported to prevent the development of very late-onset TBI-related memory deficits in mice.
Blueberry supplementation in midlife was associated with reduced memory encoding difficulty in daily life.

reports.title: Prefrontal and cingulate activity in learning, memory, and belief updating
reports.summary: The claims study prefrontal and cingulate cortex activity alongside learning, memory, and belief updating across five papers. Several claims point the same way: lateral orbitofrontal activity is associated with updating sensory representations, and lateral prefrontal activity is associated with evaluating memory. The only decrease reported is methamphetamine exposure associated with reduced belief updating in rats, so no claims directly oppose one another. Only one claim had a press match: the anterior cingulate finding was labeled understated, with press strength 2 against paper strength 3. All other claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: The anterior cingulate cortex is necessary for updating model-based strategies but not for basic reward-driven action reinforcement, and press coverage understated this claim.
Lateral orbitofrontal activity is associated with responses to unexpected outcomes, and it may contribute teaching signals that update sensory representations.
Insular, cingulate, and lateral prefrontal activation is associated with subjective recollection, and it is greater for discarded than for selected responses during decisions.
Medial prefrontal cortex populations are associated with maintaining sample information across delays.
Methamphetamine exposure in rats is associated with reduced uncertainty-driven belief updating.

reports.title: Insular cortex activation linked to recollection and semantic taste knowledge
reports.summary: These findings concern activation of the insular cortex and related regions in relation to memory recollection and semantic knowledge of food. One paper associates insular and cingulate activation with subjective recollection and with evaluation of discarded memory responses during decisions. A second paper associates food-selective insular representations with prototypical taste knowledge, even when that knowledge is task-irrelevant. All three claims are correlational (strength 1) and all report increases, so the papers agree on insular involvement without any conflicting directions. No press statements were matched to these claims, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers, and no paper is retracted.

key_findings.text: Insular activation is associated with subjective recollection in one study.
Food-selective representations in the left insula are associated with prototypical taste knowledge even when that knowledge is task-irrelevant.

reports.title: Live music, infant stroking, superior colliculus, and endopiriform neurons: unrelated topics
reports.summary: These findings cover four unrelated topics: live music and brain activity in listeners, stroking and noxious-evoked brain activity in infants, the primate superior colliculus and higher-order cognition, and endopiriform neurons and cognition in rodents. The claims do not share a common exposure or outcome, so the community is loosely linked rather than a coherent body of evidence. Within the live music paper, the claims agree in direction on increased brain activity with live music (C1) but also report brain responses partly contrary to established models (C5). Stroking is reported to decrease noxious-evoked brain activity in infants at a conditional-causal strength (C2). Press coverage is mixed: the live music press statements were overstated in one case and aligned in another, while the stroking press statements were understated in both matched cases. The superior colliculus and endopiriform claims have no press match.

key_findings.text: Live music is reported to increase brain activity in listeners, more strongly and consistently than recorded music, with the paper using conditional wording.
Stroking may decrease noxious-evoked brain activity in infants, according to the paper, and press statements understated this finding.
The primate superior colliculus is stated to mediate abstract higher-order cognition, but the direction of the relationship is unclear.
Endopiriform neurons may increase higher-order cognition, per the paper, with no press coverage matched.
Live music produces brain responses that are partly contrary to established neural models of musical emotion, a direction the paper leaves unclear.

reports.title: Axon pathology and axon length across concussion and motor neuron disease
reports.summary: The findings study axonal outcomes: axonal pathology after experimental concussion in males and females, axon loss linked to small axon caliber, and axon length in motor neuron disease models treated with synaptotagmin 13. All four claims report an increase in the studied axon measure, so no papers conflict in direction. Only one claim, C3, had a press match, and press coverage of it was understated, with press strength 1 against paper strength 3. The other three claims had no press statement matched to them, and no retracted papers are cited.

key_findings.text: Small caliber axons are linked to axon loss after concussion, with female brains showing more extensive loss because they have a higher share of small caliber axons.
Sexual dimorphism in axonal size is associated with more extensive axonal pathology in females after concussion, which may contribute to worse outcomes.
Overexpression of SYT13 in patient motor neurons in vitro increases axon length and improves survival in ALS and SMA models.

reports.title: Neural and behavioral exposures linked to recognition memory outcomes
reports.summary: These nine claims from eight papers study how neural, genetic, and behavioral exposures relate to recognition and memory outcomes. Most relationships are correlational (strength 1), with one direct causal finding (C3) and one conditional finding (C9). Directions conflict: ablating hilar somatostatin interneurons (C2) is associated with reduced recognition memory, while endopiriform projections to ventral CA1 (C8) are associated with increased recognition memory. Press coverage was overstated for C1 and C8, aligned for C3 and C7, and mixed for C9, which had three press matches. C2, C4, C5, and C6 had no matched press statement, and no papers in this community are retracted.

key_findings.text: Anti-NRXN1α autoantibodies from patients with schizophrenia reduce social novelty preference in mice, and press coverage matched this finding.
Ablation of hilar somatostatin-positive interneurons is associated with reduced recognition memory.
Endopiriform neurons projecting to ventral CA1 are associated with increased recognition memory, and press coverage overstated this finding.
Boundary-induced neural state changes during encoding are associated with higher subsequent recognition accuracy but impaired event order memory.
Repeated and varied social interactions may increase recognition consistency for familiar faces, and press coverage of this finding was mixed.

reports.title: Noradrenergic activity and hypocretin innervation in behavior and opiate withdrawal
reports.summary: This community covers noradrenergic system activity and hypocretin/orexin interactions, linked to behavioral deficits and the opiate withdrawal syndrome. The vitamin B6 deficiency paper (P1) reports that increased noradrenergic activity may drive behavioral deficits in mice, and its press coverage is labeled aligned with the paper's strength. The hypocretin paper (P2) reports no association between hypocretin neurons and adrenergic neuron number, while describing increased hypocretin innervation and tyrosine hydroxylase levels in the locus coeruleus. Only one of the two claims has a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared across this community. No retracted papers are included.

key_findings.text: Increased noradrenergic system activity may cause behavioral deficits in vitamin B6-deficient mice.
No association was found between hypocretin neurons and adrenergic neuron number, while hypocretin innervation and tyrosine hydroxylase levels in the locus coeruleus increased.

reports.title: Quality of life outcomes of light, yoga, and nerve stimulation
reports.summary: This community groups findings on quality of life as an outcome of green light exposure, chair yoga, and transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation. All four claims report an increase in quality of life, and none reports an opposing direction or a null result. The strength of wording varies: the chair yoga claim is correlational, the green light claim C1 is correlational while C4 from the same paper is direct, and the tVNS claim is direct. Press coverage is mixed: the green light claim C1 has no matched press statement, the tVNS claim C3 is aligned, and the green light claim C4 is aligned with one understated match. The chair yoga claim C2 has aligned, overstated and understated press matches.

key_findings.text: Green light exposure was associated with improved quality of life in a preliminary one-way cross-over trial of migraine patients, and GLED significantly improved quality of life and headache attacks.
Chair yoga was associated with higher quality of life than the MI group in a cluster randomized trial of community-dwelling older adults.
Two weeks of daily transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation improved some aspects of quality of life, mood and sleep in adults aged 55 or above.

reports.title: Symptom severity after concussion and post-COVID syndrome
reports.summary: This community covers studies of symptom severity as the outcome, with exposures including non-sport-related concussion, post-exertional malaise, and sex. The papers study different conditions, a concussion cohort in athletes and a post-COVID-19 case-control study in adults, so they do not directly bear on each other. Each association is reported at correlational strength only (strength 1), and all three are described as associated with greater symptom severity. Press coverage of all three findings was labelled aligned, meaning press statements matched the strength of the paper's wording. No retracted papers appear in this community.

key_findings.text: Non-sport-related concussion was associated with greater symptom severity than sport-related concussion in athletes.
Post-exertional malaise was associated with more severe symptoms and more objective signs in adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome.
Within non-sport-related concussion cases, female athletes were associated with greater symptom severity than male athletes.

reports.title: Morphine exposure effects on brain regions, EEG power, and hypocretin innervation
reports.summary: The three claims cover morphine's effects on brain structures and EEG activity in two papers, one on opiate withdrawal and one on EEG spectrogram methods. Morphine was associated with increased hypocretin innervation of the locus coeruleus, while a null result was reported for the A1/A2 medullary regions, so the two papers point in different directions on different outcomes. The EEG paper reported that morphine caused changes in EEG power at 1-3 Hz and 8-9 Hz, but the direction of those changes was unclear. No claim had a matched press statement, so press coverage cannot be compared with the papers in this community.

key_findings.text: Morphine was associated with an increase in hypocretin innervation of the locus coeruleus in mice.
Morphine caused changes in EEG power at 1-3 Hz and 8-9 Hz, with the direction of change unclear.
No association was found between morphine and the A1/A2 medullary regions.

reports.title: Chemokines and magnetic stimulation effects on neurotoxicity in neural cell studies
reports.summary: These findings concern neurotoxicity as the shared outcome, with one exposure being chemokines and the other magnetic stimulation. The chemokine paper reports a direct causal increase in neurotoxicity in neuroblastoma cells in vitro, while the magnetic stimulation paper reports no effect on neurotoxicity in FUS-ALS neurons in vitro. The two papers do not conflict directly because they study different exposures and cell systems. Press coverage of the chemokine paper understated its strength (press 1 vs paper 3), while press coverage of the magnetic stimulation null result was labeled aligned.

key_findings.text: Chemokines were reported to directly increase neurotoxicity in neuroblastoma cells in vitro.
Magnetic stimulation was reported to have no effect on neurotoxicity in FUS-ALS and healthy neurons in vitro, without obvious harmful effects.
Press coverage understated the chemokine finding relative to the paper's direct causal wording.

reports.title: Cognitive dysfunction with apathy, anxiety, APOE, and treatment outcomes
reports.summary: The 40 claims cover many papers whose shared outcome is cognitive dysfunction, with exposures including amyloid-beta pathology, APOE ε4, cardiovascular health, lifestyle, drug treatments, and cognitive rehabilitation. Most relationships are rated correlational (strength 1), while the direct causal wording comes from rehabilitation, microglial, and mouse studies. Papers agree that amyloid-beta pathology, APOE ε4, and poorer lifestyle are linked to apathy, anxiety, or cognitive impairment, and that cholinesterase inhibitors are linked to slower decline. Findings conflict on cardiovascular health, where poorer health was linked to greater decline in Black women but no association was found in White women. Of the claims with a press match, 20 are labelled aligned, 4 overstated, and 3 understated, with the overstated labels falling on the amyloid-beta and microglial papers.

key_findings.text: Amyloid-beta pathology may drive the development of apathy and anxiety in early Alzheimer's disease, and was associated with increasing apathy and anxiety over time.
Cholinesterase inhibitors were associated with slower cognitive decline, with galantamine showing the strongest effect among them.
Noradrenergic drugs produced a large positive effect on apathy in a meta-analysis and may offer effective Alzheimer's treatment for apathy and general cognition.
Poorer cardiovascular health was associated with greater cognitive decline in Black women, and no association was found in White women.
APOE ε4 was associated with higher odds of cognitive impairment and of quadruple misfolded proteins, and with lower paired-associate learning scores in family-history-positive individuals.

reports.title: Neurodegeneration in motor neuron, myelin, and dopaminergic pathways: diverse exposures
reports.summary: These five papers study factors linked to motor neuron degeneration, axonal loss, and neuronal degeneration in the vagus and brainstem. SYT13 is reported to protect motor neurons, with a conditional causal wording (strength 2), and Gemin3 is only tentatively linked to motor neuron degeneration with an unclear direction (strength 1). Myelin ensheathment is reported to increase axonal degeneration in autoimmune demyelination with direct causal wording (strength 3), and oxidative stress is reported to increase neuronal degeneration in the vagal pathway with direct causal wording (strength 3). BDNF hydrogel delivery showed no effect on motor neuron degeneration (strength 0), which is the only null result in this group, so it does not conflict with the other protective claim on the same outcome. Only the myelin claim has a press match, and press coverage of it was understated relative to the paper's strength (press 1 vs paper 3 and press 2 vs paper 3); the other claims had no press match.

key_findings.text: Synaptotagmin 13 may decrease motor neuron degeneration, and the paper calls it a candidate therapeutic target.
Myelin ensheathment increases the risk of axonal degeneration in an autoimmune environment.
Oxidative stress increases α-synuclein aggregation and degeneration of DMnX neurons.
BDNF hydrogel delivery showed no association with motor neuron degeneration, and the paper concluded that its mechanism was not neuroprotection within the spinal cord.
Gemin3 is associated with motor neuron degeneration, with an unclear direction of effect.
